current_description.description_long: The Associated Press published a review of campaign promises Donald Trump said he would address on his first day back in office. The article listed commitments including a large deportation program, closing the border, ending birthright citizenship, imposing tariffs, and pardoning some people charged or convicted in connection with the January 6, 2021 attack on the Capitol. It also distinguished campaign statements from actions a president could take unilaterally. AP noted that Congress and the courts could constrain those plans, and that some promises, such as changing birthright citizenship, could not be accomplished by executive order alone. The report therefore supports a concrete description of AP examining Trump’s Day-One pledges and their legal or practical limits. It does not document shifting evaluation criteria, repeated review cycles, a general decline in credibility, or a quantified delivery record for every campaign promise. This draft narrows the entry to the specific coverage that can be checked. The linked AP tracker should be retained only if its underlying promise rows remain accessible to reviewers.
current_description.description_medium: The Associated Press reviewed promises Donald Trump said he would carry out on his first day back in office. Its January 2025 report listed commitments on immigration, birthright citizenship, tariffs, energy and January 6 pardons, and explained that Congress and the courts could limit what a president can do alone. The report supports an account of AP’s promise review, not claims that Trump shifted criteria across repeated review cycles or that the tracker measured resulting credibility costs.

frozen_original.title: Bondi Drops DOJ Cases Against Trump Allies on Day One
frozen_original.synopsis: Attorney General Pam Bondi directed the Department of Justice to drop or suspend ongoing criminal cases and investigations against Trump allies on her first day in office, weaponizing the Justice Department as a personal protection service for the president's associates. The cases included fraud investigations, campaign finance violations, and other matters involving individuals connected to Trump. The moves confirmed fears that the DOJ under Bondi would function as a political tool rather than an independent law enforcement agency.

frozen_original.title: Trump Calls Serena Williams 'Ugly' and 'Really Bad' at Golf
frozen_original.synopsis: In August 2009, following a contentious U.S. Open semifinal match in which Serena Williams was penalized and lost a point after a heated exchange with a line judge, Trump used the incident as a springboard to make unprompted personal attacks on Williams. He wrote in a blog post that Williams 'got so ugly' on the court and called her 'a really bad person.' Trump also disparaged Williams' tennis skills and appearance in a way that commentators noted was racially coded. The attacks on one of the greatest athletes in American sports history were widely seen as reflecting Trump's broader pattern of singling out prominent Black women for derogatory personal attacks.
